summary.text: Take \(n=7\). Every allowed value of \(x\) is at least \(3\), and \(x\le y\le z\) would force \(x+y+z\ge 3x\ge 9\), contradicting \(x+y+z=7\); thus the strengthened representation clause, and hence the combined conjecture, is false.

full_proof.text:
Let a valid representation of an integer \(n\) mean a triple of positive integers
\[
x\le y\le z,\qquad x+y+z=n,
\]
for which all six integers
\[
2x-1,\quad 2y-1,\quad 2z-1,\quad 2xy-1,\quad 2xz-1,\quad 2yz-1
\]
are prime. The conjecture contains two assertions: first, that every \(n>5\) has at least one valid representation; and, moreover, that every \(n>6\) has a valid representation in which
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
We disprove the combined conjecture by showing that its “moreover” assertion fails at \(n=7\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that the conjecture is true. Since \(7>6\), its second assertion supplies positive integers \(x,y,z\) such that
\[
x+y+z=7,\qquad x\le y\le z,
\]
all six indicated numbers are prime, and
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
Membership in this finite set gives the five possible cases
\[
x=3,\quad x=4,\quad x=6,\quad x=10,\quad\text{or}\quad x=15.
\]
In particular, in every case \(x\ge 3\).

The ordering now gives
\[
y\ge x
\]
and, because \(z\ge y\ge x\), also
\[
z\ge x.
\]
Consequently,
\[
x+y+z\ge x+x+x=3x\ge 3\cdot 3=9.
\]
But the required sum is \(x+y+z=7\), so this says simultaneously
\[
7=x+y+z\ge 9,
\]
which is impossible.

Equivalently, one can see the contradiction in each of the five membership cases explicitly: the ordering forces the sum to be at least \(9,12,18,30,45\) when \(x\) is respectively \(3,4,6,10,15\), and none of these lower bounds is compatible with a sum of \(7\). Thus no ordered positive triple with the prescribed value of \(x\) can sum to \(7\), regardless of any primality conditions.

Therefore \(n=7\) is a counterexample to the claim that every integer \(n>6\) has such a representation with \(x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}\). Since that claim is a conjunct of the stated universal conjecture, its failure disproves the conjecture as a whole.
